title: Souls are not now created; Moses on God's rest
pass_a_gloss: If souls now come to be by providence rather than by creation, absurdities follow. Moses says God rested from all his works which he began to make. If God still creates souls now, then it is false that he rested from all his works. But if souls come by succession like bodies, they are mortal as other generated things are. Both alternatives are absurd; therefore souls are not now coming into being. The saying 'My Father is working' is about providence, not about creating new soul-substances.
pass_b_english: Are souls still being made? If they arise now only by providence, not by creation, the account falters. Moses says God rested from all his works which he had begun to make (Genesis 2:2). Keep creating souls today and that rest is emptied. Make them by bodily succession instead and you drag them into the mortality of generated things. Both roads are absurd; so souls are not now coming to be. When it is said 'My Father is working still' (John 5:17), the sense is providence, not minting new soul-essences.
